headline: Chip Rout Drags Stocks Lower as Housing and Energy Stand Apart
body_html:
Stocks ended Friday, October 30, firmly lower, with semiconductors at the center of the damage. Of the 532 names we track, only 175 rose while 354 fell, roughly two decliners for every advancer. The semiconductor group dropped 6.59%, and the pain reached into memory and optical networking: Sandisk lost 16.07% and Coherent gave up 13.87%.

The rotation was narrow. Homebuilders gained 1.48% and energy edged up 0.31%, the only two groups in positive territory. Everything else slid: materials fell 2.01%, industrials 1.79%, healthcare 1.34%, software 1.33% and consumer names 0.48%. Housing-linked stocks led the winners, with Cavco Industries up 11.04% and Mohawk Industries up 7.16%. Energy had a geopolitical backdrop, with reports of tankers hit in the Strait of Hormuz.

The standout mover was Capri Holdings, which jumped 15.82% to top the board. On the other side, Roblox fell 18.08% and Bright Horizons 17.86%. With a St. Louis Fed official calling for tighter policy soon and Gulf tensions unresolved, a market where losers outnumber winners this heavily goes into Monday, November 2, looking for stability.

briefs.headline: Tanker Incidents Keep Hormuz on Edge
briefs.body: Iran's naval Revolutionary Guard said three tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz. Security sources separately pointed to limpet mines on another vessel. Oman's navy also pulled 25 crew from a ship off Musandam, underscoring the strain on one of the world's key shipping lanes.

briefs.headline: Washington Pulls Some Staff From Saudi Arabia
briefs.body: The US ordered non-emergency personnel to leave Saudi Arabia, citing security risks. The move adds to the sense of unease across the Gulf. It arrived in a session when energy was one of only two groups to finish higher.

briefs.headline: Pakistan Sees a Thin Opening for Iran-US Talks
briefs.body: Pakistan's military is described as cautiously optimistic about mediating between Iran and the United States, according to Reuters. Nothing is settled, but the diplomatic track offers a counterweight to the day's maritime alarms and could shape sentiment as trading resumes Monday.

briefs.headline: Fed's Musalem Says Tighter Policy Is Needed Soon
briefs.body: St. Louis Fed president Musalem argued that monetary policy should tighten before long. Hawkish talk like this tends to weigh on richly valued growth stocks. Friday's heavy selling in chips and software fit that pattern, though no single cause was confirmed.

briefs.headline: BP Posts Record Profit, Aims to Settle Spill Bill Early
briefs.body: BP beat forecasts with a record profit and said it wants to settle its Deepwater Horizon obligations ahead of schedule. A Reuters commentary noted that the oil majors' restraint on spending says more than their earnings do, pointing to continued caution over new investment.

briefs.headline: Software and Internet Names Take Sharp Hits
briefs.body: Twilio fell 14.48% and Roblox dropped 18.08%, while the broader software group lost 1.33%. Exceptions existed: GoDaddy rose 11.06% and Donnelley Financial gained 8.10%. The split showed investors sorting individual stories rather than selling the whole space.
